bull.b: Vector’s rapid adoption and strong sequential growth indicate increasing customer engagement with Unity’s monetization platform. Reaching more than $1 billion in annual recurring revenue ahead of expectations strengthens the growth engine and could support durable operating leverage as usage expands.

bull.t: Strong cash generation and improved balance sheet
bull.b: Substantial free cash flow gives Unity internal funding for product investment while reducing reliance on external capital. The shift to a net-cash position improves resilience, supports repayment of the 2026 convertible, and creates greater flexibility to pursue strategic priorities.

bull.t: Platform innovation expands Unity’s addressable market
bull.b: The rearchitected Unity 7 platform, open development interfaces, AI tooling, and Commerce capabilities broaden the ways customers can create and monetize real-time experiences. These products can deepen platform relevance across gaming and non-gaming workflows over time.

bear.t: Persistent GAAP losses and weak returns
bear.b: Unity has not yet established sustainable GAAP profitability despite improving adjusted results. Continued operating and net losses can erode equity value, restrict financial flexibility, and make the company more dependent on successful execution before earnings become consistently durable.

Create subscriptions and tools are central to Unity’s developer ecosystem, yet their growth is materially slower than Strategic Grow. If this pattern persists, the company may face difficulty broadening growth beyond monetization products and sustaining overall platform expansion.

bear.t: Runtime data and Unity AI remain early-stage
bear.b: Future growth increasingly depends on new runtime and AI capabilities, but adoption and monetization are not yet proven. Delayed rollout and limited measurable revenue contribution create execution risk, leaving the expected benefit from these initiatives dependent on sustained customer uptake.
